subject: Renewal: SOC 2 re-attest — evidence cadence, retention carveout, and reserved-GPU uplift
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@lighthousefin.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@solstice.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal prep + retention ask

Olga — thanks for the quick run-through on Friday. As we discussed with procurement, Lighthouse is comfortable moving forward with a renewal once we have clarity on two items: (1) exact retention window for audit logs (we have a 7-year regulatory requirement for a subset of logs), and (2) whether reserved GPU capacity can be carved out and billed monthly instead of upfront for the first 6 months.

Can you share a proposed evidence cadence and an updated term amendment we can push through legal? Ideally we want a single package that covers the SOC 2 re-attestation evidence, the retention carveout language (for the regulated logs), and a path to increase GPU seats from 8 -> 16 during peak month ends.

Attachment: none on my side yet — procurement asked me to collect Redwood’s proposal first.

Thanks,
Anna Liu
Director, IT & Compliance
Lighthouse Financial
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@lighthousefin.com>, procurement@solstice.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal prep + retention ask

Anna — thanks, and appreciated the clarity. Draft plan below and I’ve looped in Kim (security/compliance) and Ben (sales lead for Lighthouse) to cover legal and billing. High-level proposal: 

1) Evidence cadence: we will deliver an evidence bundle in three batches to match your audit window — initial snapshot (T-60 days), incremental runbook (T-30 to T-7), and final consolidated packet (T-0). We’ll include the SOC 2 control matrix, sampled logs, and an index for auditors to speed review.

2) Retention carveout: we can support a 7-year retention window for a designated log class (financial transaction audit logs). This will be implemented as an archival policy with read-only escrow export capability. There is a one-time engineering mapping fee and a monthly archive storage surcharge.

3) Reserved GPU uplift: we can provision a temporary reserved pool (16 GPUs) for month-end peaks with a monthly surcharge. For smoothing cash flow, we can convert the first 6 months of the reserved commit to a month-to-month invoice and then revert to quarterly billing thereafter, subject to a short-term amendment.

I’ve attached an evidence matrix and a retention spec draft for your review. Also including a placeholder DocuSign link for the capacity amendment so procurement can see the language.

Attachments: [Attachment: SOC2_evidence_matrix_v3.xlsx (xlsx)], [Attachment: Retention_Carveout_Spec.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: ReservedGPU_Amendment_DocuSign.pdf (pdf)]

Next steps: Anna — can you confirm the specific log classes that must be retained 7 years? Procurement — if you want, we can provide a redline to your standard SOW/PO template.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer — Security Ops
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Anna Liu <anna.liu@lighthousefin.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 08:39:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal prep + retention ask

Thanks, Olga. Quick clarifications from compliance/legal POV: 

— The 7-year retention carveout will require explicit language in Section 4.2 (Data Retention) and an appendix describing export/escrow procedures. I’ll prepare a redline.
— For the evidence batches, auditors prefer hashed manifests for log samples and a summary of sampling methodology. I’ve added a column to the evidence matrix for "hash manifest" and a short methods note.
— Engineering needs concrete sampling windows (we recommend 30-minute contiguous windows across representative days) so we don’t end up pulling huge continuous dumps.

Ben — can you surface the proposed monthly surcharge numbers so procurement has a ballpark before we push a DocuSign? I can draft the legal redline by EOD Friday if we have the surcharge and mapping fee amounts.

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Anna Liu <anna.liu@lighthousefin.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2028 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal prep + retention ask

Anna / Kim / Olga — rough pricing for planning: 

— One-time engineering mapping fee: $8,500 (covers policy mapping + export connector setup)
— Monthly archive surcharge for 7-year retention (estimated): $1,400/month (based on expected ingest of ~45GB/mo of designated logs; reported as compressed archive pricing)
— Reserved GPU temporary uplift (8 additional units): $5,600/month for first 6 months if invoiced month-to-month; thereafter $4,900/month if committed quarterly.

I’ll put formal numbers into the amendment doc but we can start procurement conversation with these. Anna — are these within your budget assumptions? If not, we can explore a phased approach (e.g., archive-only for a subset of logs first).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@lighthousefin.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, procurement@solstice.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal prep + retention ask

Thanks everyone — that looks reasonable. A couple quick notes after internal review: 

1) Procurement wants the DocuSign showing monthly invoicing for the first 6 months of reserved GPUs before we sign. Can you ship the DocuSign with the monthly option visible as checkbox?
2) Compliance confirmed the exact log class: "payments.transaction.audit" and a related subset of API gateway access logs. We’ll provide a mapping document by 12/06 so you can scope the export.
3) For the evidence cadence, the Lighthouse auditors asked that the final consolidated packet include a signed SOC 2 scope statement and a CSV index of hashes for each sampled file.

If you can get the DocuSign draft + Kim’s redline by EOD 12/05, procurement will be able to route this through legal the following week.

Anna Liu
Director, IT & Compliance
Lighthouse Financial
